songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line

ai_show_review.summary: Epic Dark Star marathon & soaring Here Comes Sunshine; tight set flow
ai_show_review.blurb: The night features a monumental 43‑minute Dark Star that dominates the second set, bookended by an inspired Here Comes Sunshine. Jerry’s guitar soars while Keith’s Rhodes drives the improvisations, and Phil’s bass fuels the jams. Highlights include the classic China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider transition and a heartfelt rendition of Stella Blue.
ai_show_review.review: On December 6, 1973 at Cleveland Public Auditorium the Dead delivered one of their most memorable late‑year shows. The first set rolls through solid rockers – Bertha, Mexicali Blues, Deal – before launching into a legendary China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider segue that still gets fans talking. The second set is where the magic truly unfolds: an almost 45‑minute Dark Star erupts into Eyes Of The World and Stella Blue, all propelled by Keith’s spacey Rhodes and Phil’s thunderous bass, before closing with a joyous Here Comes Sunshine and a bright Sugar Magnolia. Across all available soundboard sources the performance feels locked in; Jerry’s tone is both powerful and lyrical, his solos on Dark Star and Here Comes Sunshine are nothing short of soaring, while Bill Kreutzmann keeps the rhythm tight and relentless. This show stands out as a high‑water mark for the 1973 tour, combining exploratory improvisation with tight songcraft, making it essential listening for any Deadhead.

best_recording.reason: Crystal‑clear soundboard mix that captures the full Dark Star and Here Comes Sunshine with minimal glitches, offering the most balanced instrument separation and overall fidelity.

key_highlights: 43‑minute Dark Star marathon that defines the second set
Extended, soaring Here Comes Sunshine anchoring the show
Seamless Dark Star → Eyes Of The World → Stella Blue sequence
Iconic China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider transition

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers inspired, soaring solos—especially on Here Comes Sunshine and throughout the epic Dark Star—with a powerful tone and lyrical phrasing that drives the improvisations.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh’s bass is thunderous and super‑energetic, providing the backbone for the long jams and adding melodic bursts that lift the Dark Star and subsequent transitions.
band_performance.Bob: Weir supplies solid rhythm guitar and clear vocal contributions; his playing supports the extended jams while staying in the mix during the lengthy Dark Star.
band_performance.Keith: Godchaux’s Rhodes/electric piano is a spacey, jazzy catalyst for the night, shaping the texture of Dark Star and adding warm piano flavor on Big River and other cuts.
band_performance.Mickey: Hart offers a steady, unobtrusive foundation that blends smoothly with the band, contributing subtle accents throughout the set.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann is ‘on fire,’ delivering relentless propulsion and powerful drumming—especially evident on the marathon jams like Dark Star and Big River.
